chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a man reciting in the obligatory prayer only Fatihat al-Kitab in the first two rak'ahs when a need has pressed him or something occurs.

key_terms.أَعْجَلَتْ بِهِ حَاجَةٌ: a need has pressed or hurried him
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ: the first two rak'ahs of the prayer
key_terms.بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: with Fatihat al-Kitab; meaning Surat al-Fatihah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite only Fatihat al-Kitab in an obligatory prayer when there is an urgent need?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal concession in obligatory prayer: it is permissible to recite only Fatihat al-Kitab in the first two rak'ahs when one is pressed by a need or an unexpected matter arises. Its significance lies in showing ease and practical flexibility within the rulings of salat under constrained circumstances.
